entries.title: The support assistant is not responding
entries.meaning: The assistant panel accepted your message but no answer came back. This is a transport or backend problem, not a problem with the wording of your question.
likely_causes: The backend API is not running (or was restarted) at the address the frontend is configured with.
The request is taking longer than the client waits — for example a first request that is still warming the embedding model.
The browser blocked the request (network, extension, or mixed content), so nothing reached the server.
steps: Check the assistant's own error line — it distinguishes a network failure from a server error.
Open GET /api/support/health in a browser tab. It reports whether the API process and the support knowledge base are actually available.
If the API is not reachable, start it from backend/ with: uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
Press Retry on the failed message rather than retyping it.
If health is fine but the assistant still fails, copy the exact error text and report it.
entries.retry: Yes — retry is appropriate here, and the message keeps its place in the conversation when you press Retry.
entries.escalate: Report the support health payload (GET /api/support/health) and the exact error text from the panel. Do not paste API keys or tokens.

entries.title: The backend is unavailable
entries.meaning: The frontend could not get a usable response from the FastAPI backend, so it has no data to show. Nothing is wrong with the legal corpus itself.
likely_causes: The API process is not running, or is listening on a different port than the frontend expects.
VITE_API_BASE points somewhere the browser cannot reach.
A deployment is mid-restart, or a hosted instance is waking from idle.
steps: Check GET /api/health on the same origin the frontend uses. A JSON payload with a document count means the API is alive.
Locally, confirm the API is running: uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000 from backend/.
Confirm frontend/.env.local VITE_API_BASE matches that origin, then restart the dev server (Vite only reads env vars at startup).
Use the assistant's Retry button once the API answers.
entries.retry: Retry only after the health check answers. Retrying against a down API will keep failing.
entries.escalate: Report the health URL you checked, the status it returned, and whether you are running locally or against a deployment.

entries.title: The request timed out
entries.meaning: The request was accepted but did not finish inside the allowed time. The work may have been partially done.
likely_causes: The first request after startup warms the embedding model and can take noticeably longer.
The LLM provider was slow or unreachable (LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defaults to 45).
A very large query or a large top_k increased retrieval work.
steps: Wait a few seconds and press Retry — the second attempt usually runs against a warm model.
Shorten the query and lower the result count if you set one.
Check GET /api/support/health to see whether the LLM is even configured; retrieval answers without it.
If it reproduces on a short query with a warm model, treat it as a backend problem and report it.
entries.retry: Yes, once. Repeated long waits suggest the provider or the machine is the bottleneck.
entries.escalate: Report the query length, whether the answer eventually arrived, and whether LLM_PROVIDER is configured (not the key itself).

entries.title: Results appear but there is no generated summary
entries.meaning: Retrieval is live and working, but no language model is configured, so the system shows the retrieved passages instead of writing prose. This is the documented fallback, not an error.
likely_causes: No provider key is set in backend/.env (HF_API_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
A key is present but is a placeholder, so it is deliberately ignored.
LLM_PROVIDER names a provider whose key is not set.
steps: Check GET /api/support/health — it reports whether an LLM provider is configured, without exposing the value.
To enable generation, set LLM_PROVIDER and the matching key in backend/.env, then restart the API.
Until then, use the retrieved sources directly: they are the same evidence the model would have been given.
Note the answer source label in the response — it says whether the text was generated or came from retrieval only.
entries.retry: No — retrying will not change the outcome until a key is configured.
entries.escalate: Report that generation is disabled and which provider you expect. Never paste the key itself into the chat.

entries.title: Rate limit or quota exceeded
entries.meaning: Something in the chain refused the request because a limit was reached — either the LLM provider's quota or the assistant's own feedback/request throttle.
likely_causes: The provider's free tier or monthly quota is exhausted.
Many requests were made in a short window (for example from a shared machine or a demo session).
The assistant's feedback endpoint was posted repeatedly.
steps: Wait a minute before retrying; short bursts recover quickly.
Reduce repeated identical requests — ask one clear question instead of several near-duplicates.
If the provider's quota is exhausted, research still works: retrieval and sources do not need the LLM.
For feedback, submit once — repeats are throttled on purpose.
entries.retry: Yes, after a pause. Immediately repeating a throttled request will fail again.
entries.escalate: Report the provider name, roughly how many requests you made, and the time window. Never paste the key.

entries.title: The legal search returned no results
entries.meaning: The retrieval ran, but nothing in the indexed corpus matched closely enough with the current filters.
likely_causes: The query is very specific, so no single stored chunk is close to it.
A Court or Year filter is narrower than you expect — filters come from the corpus and are easy to leave set.
The topic is outside this corpus, which covers 100 Indian Supreme Court judgment PDFs.
steps: Press Reset on the filter panel to clear Court and Year, then search again.
Search the legal principle rather than the exact facts ('wrongful termination damages' rather than a long narrative).
Try the statutory provision you have in mind, for example 'IPC Section 302'.
Broaden one step at a time and watch the match count change.
If a topic returns nothing even unfiltered, it is simply not in this corpus.
entries.retry: Yes, with a modified query or cleared filters. Repeating the identical query will return the identical result.
entries.escalate: Report the exact query text, the filters in use, and the match count. That is enough to tell 'absent topic' from 'retrieval bug'.

entries.title: Missing or unverifiable source citations
entries.meaning: The answer did not carry citations you can check. Either nothing was retrieved, or generation was disabled and the answer is a retrieval listing rather than a cited summary.
likely_causes: Retrieval returned nothing, so there were no chunks to cite.
The response was a low-confidence payload, which reports sources but generates no answer and no citations.
No LLM is configured, so the text is a deterministic listing labelled as such.
steps: Check the response's answer source label: 'retrieved sources only' is not the same as a generated summary.
Look at the retrieved records themselves — they carry chunk ids and source filenames even when the answer cites nothing.
Verify a specific record with GET /api/research/chunk/{chunk_id}.
If the answer cites a source that is not in the retrieved list, treat that citation as unverified and tell the maintainers.
entries.retry: Only after changing the query or the filters. Retrying the same query returns the same empty citation set.
entries.escalate: Report the query, the chunk ids you could verify, and the citation text that did not verify.

entries.title: The request was rejected as invalid
entries.meaning: Input validation refused the request before any retrieval or generation ran. Nothing was searched.
likely_causes: The message or query was empty, or shorter than the required minimum (research queries need at least 2 characters).
A field was the wrong length — for example a scenario position over the allowed size, or an oversized message.
A numeric field was outside its allowed range (top_k must be 1–50).
steps: Read the validation message: it names the field and the rule.
For research, write a real question rather than a single character.
For the Compare tab, keep each scenario position to a normal paragraph and fill in the legal issue.
Resubmit — a corrected request is not charged or throttled.
entries.retry: Yes, immediately, once the named field is corrected.
entries.escalate: Report the field name and the rule from the message. Legal terminology in a question is never a validation error by itself.

entries.title: Authentication or session problems
entries.meaning: The workspace session is missing or expired, so the app returned you to the sign-in screen.
likely_causes: The session expired — 12 hours for a session-storage sign-in.
You signed in without 'Remember me', so the session lived in sessionStorage and the tab or browser was closed.
Browser data was cleared, or a different browser/profile is being used.
The app is running in demo mode, where credentials are validated locally and no server session exists.
steps: Sign in again; use 'Remember me' to keep the session in localStorage across restarts.
Check whether the sign-in screen says demo mode — if it does, authentication is not connected to a server in this build and there is no reset flow to look for.
Sign out deliberately before switching accounts, so the old session does not linger.
If a configured endpoint rejects valid credentials, report the HTTP status the screen showed.
entries.retry: Yes — signing in again is the intended recovery.
entries.escalate: Report whether the screen showed demo or live mode and the status code, if any. Never send a password.

entries.title: Theme or interface rendering problems
entries.meaning: The interface is rendering with the wrong appearance, or a control is missing. Theme state is local to your browser, so a stale stored preference is a common cause.
likely_causes: A stored palette or mode from an earlier version is still being applied.
The operating system appearance changed while the app was set to 'System default'.
A custom palette was saved with low-contrast colours.
The browser window is narrow, so a responsive layout moved or hid a control.
steps: Open Settings, then choose Light or Dark explicitly rather than leaving 'System default'.
Pick a standard palette again to overwrite a custom one, then re-apply your colours.
Reload the page; theme tokens are applied on load.
Resize the window to check whether the control is only rearranged at narrow widths.
The reading view has its own independent theme — set it there rather than in Settings.
entries.retry: Not applicable — this is a settings and rendering issue, not a request that can be retried.
entries.escalate: Report the mode and palette selected, the browser, and a screenshot description. Note whether the reader theme is also affected.

entries.title: Network error reaching the backend
entries.meaning: The request never completed at the network layer. The browser reports it as a network failure rather than an HTTP status, so the server may never have seen it.
likely_causes: The API is not running or is on a different origin than VITE_API_BASE.
Cross-origin access was refused — the backend allows localhost on any port and *.vercel.app, plus anything in CORS_ORIGINS.
The machine is offline, behind a proxy, or a browser extension is blocking the request.
Mixed content: an HTTPS page calling an HTTP API.
steps: Open the API's health URL directly in a browser tab. If that fails too, the problem is not the app.
Confirm the frontend origin is allowed by the backend CORS configuration.
Restart the Vite dev server after changing VITE_API_BASE — it is read at startup only.
Disable extensions briefly, or try a private window, to rule out a blocker.
Check the browser console for the exact blocked request before reporting.
entries.retry: Yes, after fixing the origin or bringing the API up. Retrying without that will fail identically.
entries.escalate: Report the API origin, the frontend origin, and the browser console message.

entries.title: A browser feature is unavailable
entries.meaning: The browser does not expose an API the feature needs, so the feature cannot run. The rest of the application is unaffected.
likely_causes: The browser does not implement the Web Speech API (or only the prefixed variant).
Microphone permission was denied, or no input device is present.
The page is served over an insecure origin, which blocks microphone access.
steps: Use typing instead of dictation — every field accepts typed input and nothing is lost.
For voice, use a current Chromium-based browser and serve the app over https or localhost.
Re-check site permissions for microphone in the browser's address-bar settings.
Confirm a microphone is actually connected if the browser reports no input device.
entries.retry: Yes for the typed workflow. For voice, retry only after changing browser or permissions.
entries.escalate: Report the browser name and version and the exact message the feature displayed.
